title: Resolve console usage analytics drift: per-model charts showing delayed/backfilled tokens
creator: Maya Li
description: Overview: The Console usage dashboards (per-model token/embedding breakdowns and per-route cost charts) are intermittently showing lower totals during business hours with compensating spikes several hours later. Backfilled rows appear in the datastore (ClickHouse/Redshift) with ingestion timestamps that place them after the reporting window, causing dashboards to show stale or inaccurate daily totals and per-model shares. This ticket captures the investigation, proposed remediation, and deployment plan to ensure charts reflect correct "as-of" usage and to add instrumentation for future regressions.
reproduction_steps: 1) Load the console and select the last 24h range; observe per-model percentages and total tokens for the day.
2) Query the raw usage_events table for event_time and ingestion_time for a specific model (e.g., openai/ambiguous-v1) over the same 24h window.
3) Filter events where ingestion_time > event_time + 2 hours; note counts and token totals.
4) Re-run after 6 hours; note the console totals increase as backfills are processed and appear in the boxplot/time-series.
5) Confirm that the console aggregates currently use ingestion_time as the grouping key rather than event_time or event_time with watermarking.
6) Run the reconciliation query (see monitoring_queries) to compute delta between accounted tokens and raw event tokens.
7) Observe duplicate upserts caused by non-idempotent batch inserts during reprocessing windows (consumer retry path).
investigation_notes: - Initial triage (2026-02-26): Alerts from billing team reported mismatches between ledger totals and console daily charts; discrepancy ~1.2% on average, up to 6% during heavy reprocess windows.

- Data flow: Events emitted from inference proxies -> Kafka topic `usage-events` -> stream processor (Beam) -> materialized aggregates in ClickHouse; hourly backfill job writes to same table via bulk upsert.
- Observed incorrect aggregation key: frontend aggregate queries currently join on ingestion_time_bucket (hour) which reflects CDC/backfill arrival time.

- Consumer behavior: Under consumer restart, Beam pipeline replays a batch with deduplication disabled for a small idempotency key, causing duplicate records for the same event_id when backfill runs overlap with live ingestion.
- Watermarking absent: The streaming job doesn't set an event-time watermark threshold; late events are accepted and appended using ingestion_time, creating time-travel artifacts in the hourly cube.

- Example incident: 2026-03-02 11:00-14:00 spike in 'backfilled' rows after a re-run of the 24h reprocessing job; console showed artificial drop during the window because those events were counted in later buckets.
- Initial hypothesis validated by running event_time vs ingestion_time aggregates and diffing daily totals.
- Risks: Immediate fixes to queries could mask delayed writes; need to ensure historical correction (backfill reprocessing) and prevent double-counting.
root_cause: Aggregation and consumer semantics: console aggregate queries used ingestion_time buckets rather than event_time with allowed lateness; streaming pipeline lacked watermarking and idempotent writes leading to duplicates during backfill/replay windows.
proposed_solution: 1) Change Console aggregation queries to use event_time (the canonical timestamp) and apply a configurable 'allowed_lateness' window for the UI (default 2h) so users see an "as-of" indicator and can choose to include late-arriving data.
2) Update stream processing (Beam) to set event-time watermarks and drop or route late events to a 'late_events' table instead of main aggregates unless within allowed_lateness.
3) Make bulk backfill jobs idempotent: switch to upsert by event_id and add a last_seen_at column; ensure deduplication on write (ClickHouse MergeTree TTL or Redshift idempotent loader pattern).
4) Implement a one-off reconciliation and correction run for the past 14 days to fix per-day totals; write a delta report and retain audit trail rows with backfill_reason tag.
5) Add console UI changes: show 'data_freshness' badge per-chart, provide a toggle to include/exclude late events, and surface notes when reconciliations change historical totals.
6) Add monitoring: daily reconciliation job, alert when delta > 0.5% for 3 consecutive days, and SLO for data completeness.
7) Add e2e test harness that simulates late events and replays to ensure no duplication and correct charting behavior.
8) Coordinate with Billing/Finance to validate ledger alignment after reconciliation.
9) Document changes in runbook and release notes for customers (Private/Dedicated users may have different ingestion guarantees).
10) Estimate: 5 engineering points + 2 QA points + 1 operations run for reconciliation.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Deploy query change in staging console to use event_time with allowed_lateness=2h; run for 48h and compare totals to raw events.
Phase 2 (pipeline): Deploy Beam watermarking and idempotent write logic to a single consumer shard; run backfill correction dry-run.
Phase 3 (reconciliation): Execute historical correction for last 14 days in a maintenance window; write audit logs and delta report to S3.
Phase 4 (UI): Release data_freshness indicators and toggle to 10% of accounts (feature flag).
Phase 5 (global): Flip feature flag after 48h of stability; monitor reconciliation alerts for 7 days.
Rollback: Revert console query to previous ingestion_time aggregation and pause reconciliation if new duplicates are observed.
Owners: Data infra (Carlos Mendes) + Billing lead (Aisha Patel) + Console frontend (Luca Romano).
ETA: 2 weeks to full roll-out, with critical fixes in 72h for canary.
Maintenance window: Schedule reconciliation on 2026-03-18 02:00-04:00 UTC to minimize impact on reporting.
Communications: Post-mortem and customer note to be published after reconciliation completes; notify sales for any enterprise customers with custom SLAs.
acceptance_criteria: Console per-model daily totals match raw event_time aggregates within 0.1% for last 7 days after reconciliation.
No duplicate event_ids exist in main aggregate table (run uniqueness query).
Data_freshness indicator displays correct as-of time and toggling late-events yields expected deltas.
Reconciliation job produces delta report and SLO alerting is operational.
Billing ledger alignment: finance confirms charges match reconciled totals for a sample of customers.
E2E test covers late-arrival scenarios and fails if duplication occurs.
QA signoff obtained and PRs merged.
monitoring_queries: SELECT date(event_time) AS day, sum(tokens) AS event_tokens FROM usage_events WHERE event_time >= now() - interval '14 day' GROUP BY day ORDER BY day;
SELECT date(ingestion_time) AS day, sum(tokens) AS ingestion_tokens FROM usage_events WHERE ingestion_time >= now() - interval '14 day' GROUP BY day ORDER BY day;
-- Uniqueness check: find duplicate event_ids in main aggregate table:
SELECT event_id, count(*) FROM usage_aggregates WHERE day >= current_date - 14 GROUP BY event_id HAVING count(*) > 1;
SELECT day, event_tokens, ingestion_tokens, (event_tokens - ingestion_tokens) AS delta FROM ( /* subqueries above */ );
-- Alert query: trigger if abs(delta)/event_tokens > 0.005 for 3 consecutive days.
-- Streaming health: Beam watermark lag metric: beam.watermark_lag_seconds > 300 -> warn.
